clue.text: Expect big firm to bring worker and head together

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect
ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was once Britain's biggest industrial firm
pate is an old word for the head, especially its crown

explanation.surface: A large company plans to unite its labour force with its management.
explanation.walkthrough: Imperial Chemical Industries was a former British industrial giant; 'bring together' is a picture of the firm sitting between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to look forward to it as likely, a synonym of expect.

clue.text: Aspires to produce excellent script

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a handwritten script

explanation.surface: A writer hopes to turn out a first-class screenplay.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is read with the digit 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who aims at a goal strives or hopes to reach it.

clue.text: Vehicle that's brown and khaki primarily?

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: primarily means take only the opening letter of the word khaki

explanation.surface: A question about a military vehicle painted in drab brown and khaki.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank is an armoured military vehicle running on tracks.

clue.text: Penny possibly embraces me with these welcoming words

indicators.note: embraces means the coin word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a penny is one example of a coin, hence 'possibly'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny hugs the speaker while greeting them warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name, but it is the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to invite a visitor through the door, a spoken greeting.

clue.text: See toper gain favour, reformed as very moral person

indicators.note: reformed means re-formed, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Watch a drunkard win approval by mending his ways and becoming a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is just a link at the start; 'reformed' rearranges TOPER GAIN FAVOUR. The pun is that a reformed toper is exactly such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect model, so a paragon of virtue is someone of exemplary goodness.

clue.text: Most of the quarrel comes from parsimony

indicators.note: most of means drop the last letter of the word the

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
a rift is a falling-out or quarrel

explanation.surface: Most rows arise from someone being stingy with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift is careful economy with money, a synonym for parsimony.

clue.text: See drunkard outside front of pub

indicators.note: outside means the drunkard word goes around the other letter

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard

indicators.note: front of means the opening letter of the word pub

explanation.surface: Look at the drunk standing outside the pub entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or catch sight of it.

clue.text: Holy spinster going out in formal suits

parts.note: pi is a short form of pious, meaning holy or sanctimonious

indicators.note: going out suggests the letters of spinster are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A devout unmarried woman steps out in smart businesswear.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) is followed by NSTRIPES, an anagram of SPINSTER prompted by 'going out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinstripes are suits of cloth with thin stripes, the traditional formal business wear.

clue.text: Economy fare?

parts.note: reads like a cheap travel ticket, but means a set-price restaurant menu, the thrifty way to eat

explanation.surface: A question about a cheap ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed-price set meal is cheaper than ordering from the full menu, so it is economical food.

clue.text: Art men 'mort' sadly — did they work here?

indicators.note: sadly signals the words are in a bad state, so their letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Artists are dead, alas; is this where they painted?
explanation.walkthrough: MONTMARTRE is the Paris hill district famed for its painters; 'mort' is French for dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris quarter was home to many painters, so 'they', the art men, worked there.

clue.text: Ignore point put by son

parts.note: the nub is the central point of a matter

explanation.surface: Someone disregards an argument made by their son.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to rebuff or deliberately disregard them.

clue.text: One's fingertips are in a hazardous position

definitions.text: One's fingertips are in a hazardous position

parts.words: One's fingertips are in a hazardous position
parts.note: fingertips sit at the very end of an arm, a body part, just as the risky place is the far end of a tree branch

explanation.surface: A climber's hands are dangerously placed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a risky, exposed situation, like someone at the end of a branch.

clue.text: Causing worker to be late

parts.note: whoever is behind something is responsible for causing it
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Something makes an employee arrive late for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand means behind schedule, overdue or tardy.

clue.text: Engagement broken? Stop communicating

definitions.meaning: a broken engagement means the betrothal band comes off the finger
to end a telephone call by hanging up

explanation.surface: After a broken engagement, one partner stops talking to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging up a telephone ends a conversation; whimsically, a called-off betrothal sees the band removed.

clue.text: Modernisation that goes on in library

definitions.meaning: bringing something up to date, refurbishment
borrowers extend their loan of books at a library

explanation.surface: Updating that is happening inside the library.
explanation.definitionFit: Restoration brings things up to date, and extending a book loan is the library sense.

clue.text: School fete with LSD being bandied about!

indicators.note: being bandied about means tossed around, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school fair where drugs are being passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: FELSTED is an independent school in Essex, England. LSD is also old British money (pounds, shillings, pence).
explanation.definitionFit: Felsted is the name of a well-known English boarding school.

clue.text: A female Parisian archdeacon would be odd

parts.note: in French, 'a' before a feminine noun is une
Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman and a senior cleric would make a strange pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A female Parisian' suggests a woman, but it means the French feminine word for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven numbers are odd ones, not divisible by two.

clue.text: Get cutters — the golfer's starting point must come first

indicators.note: must come first places the golfer's word ahead of the other piece

parts.note: each hole begins from the tee
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to a golfer about where to start a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutters' are teeth, cutting through the gums.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby cutting its first incisors is said to be growing them through the gums.

clue.text: Author Tom loved his girl inordinately

indicators.note: inordinately means beyond proper order, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer called Tom was excessively devoted to his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Goldsmith was an 18th-century Irish writer of The Vicar of Wakefield and She Stoops to Conquer.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldsmith was an Irish novelist, playwright and poet, a writer.

clue.text: A new member of the cathedral staff within range

parts.note: the dean heads a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A newly appointed cleric joins a cathedral team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' is a mountain range, not a span or a cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things of the great South American mountain chain.

clue.text: Description of creed seen as square outside the church

indicators.note: outside means the square word surrounds the church letters

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A creed viewed as old-fashioned, kept outside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like 'old-fashioned', but means a square number.
explanation.definitionFit: The creed agreed at the Council of Nicaea is known by this adjective.

clue.text: Sorrowful female wearing hat

indicators.note: wearing means the hat word goes around the other letter as clothing does

parts.note: a beret is a soft round flat hat

explanation.surface: A grieving woman in a beret.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means bereaved and desolate, grieving a loss.

clue.text: Chaotic situation in which item of furniture gets hit

parts.note: a bed is a piece of bedroom furniture
to lam is to thrash or strike

explanation.surface: A rowdy scene in which some furniture is struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam is uproar and confusion, named after a London asylum.

clue.text: Collaborated with redesign of dailies

indicators.note: a redesign reworks the letters of dailies into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone worked together on giving the newspapers a new look.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to cooperate and communicate with others.

clue.text: Country institute had a course

parts.note: a river ran, flowing along its course

explanation.surface: A national institute ran an educational programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia.

clue.text: Mark's wrongful deed drinking gallons

definitions.note: read as 'mark is', the noun sense

indicators.note: drinking means the deed word takes the other letter inside it

parts.note: a sin is a wrongful act

explanation.surface: A man named Mark does wrong by drinking heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, but it is the definition: a mark or token.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a mark or symbol indicating something.

clue.text: Jelly runs under the stove

indicators.note: under places the runs letter below the stove in this down clue

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of heavy cast-iron range cooker
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A jelly drips down beneath the kitchen range.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed, used to set food and grow cultures.

clue.text: Scattered all over the place as pilots on mission?

definitions.meaning: airmen dispatched on a sortie are dispatched airborne

explanation.surface: Airmen dispersed widely during an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Things knocked hard are flung about, and aircrew are despatched into the air.

clue.text: Ordered a daughter to be put outside

indicators.note: put outside means the second piece is placed around the first, here the reverse

parts.note: be is the verb taken from 'to be'

explanation.surface: Someone commanded a daughter to be sent out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be put outside' means BE goes around A and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Bade is a past tense of bid, meaning commanded.

clue.text: Something decisive to put off man in pit

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put off
a miner works down a coal pit

explanation.surface: Something that discourages a coal worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A determiner is something that settles or fixes an outcome.
